question.title: Will a US governor, congressperson or cabinet member formally declare a 2028 presidential run before 2027?

research:
## Web research
**Briefing: will a sitting governor, member of Congress or cabinet member file an FEC Form 2 for the 2028 presidency before 2027?**

**1. Current status (as of Nov 24, 2026): not met, and undecided on current information.**
- No major-party figure has formally declared or filed. 2028tracker.com says that as of Nov 23, no major-party candidate has formally declared a 2028 presidential campaign. It lists only minor filers.
- Both Yahoo and 2028tracker (Nov 22) say no one has formally declared yet on the Democratic side.
- Examples of minor filers: Royce White, a former NBA player, announced on Aug 12 and filed with the FEC on Sept 21, 2026. Christopher Campbell, a Kentucky Senate candidate in the midterms, filed on Nov 12. Neither holds a qualifying office.
- Candidates who say they are considering a run, and their stated timing:
  - **Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA):**
    - He told MS NOW (about Nov 13–14) he is "strongly considering" a run.
    - He said the midterm results made it "more likely than not" that he runs.
    - He says he'll decide "after the holidays." That points to January 2027 or later, which falls outside the window.
    - Allies launched a "Run Ro" draft committee on Nov 5–6. Politico reported Khanna was not directly involved.
  - **Sen. Mark Kelly (D-AZ):** On Oct 28 he said he was "considering" a run and would decide after the election, "at the appropriate time."
  - **Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE):** He confirmed on Nov 19 that he is considering a bid and plans to visit Iowa and New Hampshire. He is retiring from the House, so confirm whether he is still a sitting member on the filing date.
  - **Sen. John Kennedy (R-LA):** On Nov 23 he said he'd run only on a "spontaneous moment of questionable genius," but cautioned it's unlikely.
  - **Pete Buttigieg:** He holds no qualifying office (former cabinet member).
  - **Gov. Andy Beshear (D-KY):** IVN says he may be the most likely candidate to announce before the end of the year, if he plans to run, citing Kalshi bettors.
  - **Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA):** His team says he will decide after the midterms, per 2028tracker. 2028tracker also says Newsom disclosed a federal investigation in June 2026.
- I found no report of any qualifying official scheduling a launch before Dec 31.

**2. Resolution source.**
- No source is named beyond the FEC Form 2, the Statement of Candidacy. I could not query FEC.gov directly.
- Proxies:
  - 2028tracker.com says 2 candidates have formally filed, both minor long-shots (Nov 18 and Nov 23 updates).
  - Ballotpedia counted 175 candidates filed with the FEC as of Aug 25, 2025, mostly independents or minor-party filers.
- Note that Form 2 is filed when someone becomes a candidate, meaning they have raised or spent more than $5,000. Registration is required within 15 days of passing $5,000. A verbal announcement therefore often comes with a filing, but an exploratory committee, or a Form 2 filed after a delay, could differ.
- A fringe sitting member who files quietly would also count. I found none.

**3. Base rate.**
- From memory, not verified in this search: no sitting governor, senator, representative or cabinet member formally launched a presidential campaign before January of the year before the election in 2016, 2020 or 2024.
  - 2016: Ted Cruz was first, in March 2015.
  - 2020: Per Wikipedia, Rep. John Delaney announced on July 28, 2017, but he was a *former* congressman by then. Tulsi Gabbard, a sitting House member, announced in January 2019 (Jan 11, 2019). Elizabeth Warren formed an exploratory committee on Dec 31, 2018.
  - 2024: Trump announced on Nov 15, 2022. He was a former president and held no office, so he would not count.
- The 2008 cycle had earlier launches. From memory, Gov. Tom Vilsack (Nov 2006) and Rep. Dennis Kucinich (Dec 2006) both launched before January 2007. Treat that as unverified.
- Polymarket's market page notes: announcements typically cluster 12–18 months before primaries, leaving limited time before 2027 for early movers.
- The base rate for a sitting official filing in the first ~8 weeks after a midterm is low, roughly 0–1 of the last 4 cycles.

**4. Scheduled events before Jan 1, 2027.**
- There is no hard trigger.
- Khanna's "after the holidays" timeline points to early 2027.
- Possible catalysts:
  - Post-midterm Democratic momentum.
  - A draft effort.
  - The DNC's Nov 23 announcement of 12 debates, five of them in 2027. Candidate criteria will come in January, and the first two debates are in June and July 2027.
  - Beshear and Bacon travel plans.
- DeSantis is term-limited with his term ending in 2027. The Florida governor-elect is Byron Donalds.
- Not checked: whether Mark Kelly or other senators have scheduled early-state trips.

**5. Markets and forecasters.**
- The Polymarket "Who will announce Presidential run before 2027?" market has 71+ outcomes. The snippets I found are inconsistent and partly stale.
  - An Aug 2026 snapshot had Kamala Harris as frontrunner at 11%.
  - Early Oct: Newsom at 14%.
  - A Nov 3 snapshot showed Beshear 28%, Gabbard 24% and Buttigieg 20%. It also labeled Rahm Emanuel as frontrunner at 56%, which looks like a scraping artifact. I could not verify these.
  - July 2026: Polymarket said Trump was the favorite to announce by year-end, at 15%.
- Important caveat: Polymarket's "announce" market resolves on an announcement alone. An announcement is sufficient for a "Yes," whether or not a nomination is filed. This question requires a Form 2 and a sitting office.
- The Kalshi and Polymarket "first Democrat to announce" odds I found are dated July 2026. Khanna 15%, Newsom 14%.
- Methodshop (Nov 10) cites strategists saying campaign machinery will be moving by Thanksgiving 2026. That is speculative.
- Manifold has a Newsom timing market. The snippet suggests most likely dates are 2027 or 2028 (before Mar 31, 2028 most likely).
- I could not retrieve a clean current aggregate probability for this specific question.

**6. Strongest evidence on each side.**

*Yes:*
- The midterms are over and candidates said they'd decide after them.
- Khanna says "more likely than not," has a draft committee, and has been touring early states.
- Many sitting officials are openly weighing runs: Kelly, Bacon, Beshear, Khanna.
- The Polymarket "before 2027" market has had double-digit prices on several names.
- A long tail of possible filers exists, including a fringe member filing quietly.

*No:*
- As of Nov 23 no major figure has filed.
- The only stated timeline (Khanna) is "after the holidays."
- The question window is about 5 weeks and includes Thanksgiving and Christmas.
- Historical norms put top-tier launches in the first half of the year before the election.
- Several contenders, such as Newsom, are term-limited or still serving in office. Newsom's term runs until January 2027, and he has weak incentive to file early.
- The 2028tracker site says most top-tier announcements are expected in 2027 or early 2028.
- Announcements without a Form 2, or exploratory committees, would not count.

**Gaps:** I could not check FEC.gov directly. I could not verify current Kalshi or Polymarket prices after Nov 3. A 2028tracker snippet saying "He announced a presidential campaign the next day" was unattributed, and I could not identify who it refers to.

slots.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 5 weeks, until December 31, 2026, with Thanksgiving and Christmas inside the window.

(b) Status quo: No. No sitting governor, senator, House member or cabinet member has filed a Form 2 for the 2028 presidential race. The only filers are minor candidates who hold no qualifying office.

(c) No scenario: Contenders such as Khanna, Beshear, Newsom, Kelly and Bacon keep "considering" through the holidays and hold any launch until January 2027 or later. That timing gives them a full first fundraising quarter and follows the usual pattern. Any December move takes the form of a PAC, a book tour, or an exploratory step without a Form 2.

(d) Yes scenario: One qualifying official decides to be first in. This could be a long-shot House member seeking attention, a retiring member like Bacon filing before leaving office on January 3, or a contender like Beshear or Khanna moving up their timeline and filing in December.

Rationale: The base rate for a sitting official filing this early is low but not zero. From memory, in the 2008 cycle Vilsack and Kucinich launched in late 2006, and in the 2020 cycle John Delaney filed in 2017 while still a sitting congressman (the research note calling him "former" appears to be wrong). The 2012, 2016 and 2024 cycles had no such early filing by a sitting official.

For this cycle, several things point to No:
- The only stated timeline, Khanna's, is "after the holidays," which falls outside the window.
- No qualifying official has a launch scheduled before December 31.
- A December filing produces a tiny, unflattering fourth-quarter fundraising report, so serious candidates usually wait until January or later.
- The question requires an actual Form 2 from someone in office at the time of filing, which is stricter than a verbal announcement.

The remaining Yes probability comes from the long tail of roughly 600 qualifying officials, any one of whom could file quietly or unexpectedly.

Probability: 4%

(a) Time left: about 5 weeks. The window closes on Dec 31, 2026, and a check of FEC filings shortly after will settle it.

(b) Status quo: No. As of Nov 23, no sitting governor, senator, House member or cabinet member has filed a Form 2 for 2028; the only filers are minor candidates who hold no qualifying office.

(c) No scenario: Contenders such as Khanna, Kelly, Beshear and Newsom spend the holidays consulting family and donors and hold formal launches for early-to-mid 2027, as is the modern norm. Khanna has said he will decide "after the holidays". Any late-December move takes the form of an exploratory committee or a verbal announcement without a Form 2 before Jan 1.

(d) Yes scenario: A sitting official tries to get ahead of a crowded open field after the midterms and files a Form 2 in December. The model is Gov. Tom Vilsack, who launched in November 2006. Candidates would be a long-shot House member such as Khanna moving early, a retiring member such as Bacon filing before leaving office, or Beshear. A fringe sitting member filing quietly would also count.

**Rationale**

- **Base rate is low but not zero.** From memory, late-year filings by sitting officials occurred in the 2008 cycle (Vilsack, and Kucinich in December 2006) and arguably in 2020 (Warren's exploratory committee on Dec 31, 2018). I recall none in the 2012, 2016 or 2024 cycles. That is roughly 1–2 of the last 5 cycles, and 2028 resembles 2008 in being open on both sides.
- **No concrete signal of a launch.** No qualifying official has scheduled an announcement before Dec 31, and the only stated timeline (Khanna) points to January or later.
- **The window is short and awkward.** It spans Thanksgiving and Christmas, when campaigns rarely launch.
- **The bar is narrower than "announcing."** It requires an actual Form 2 from someone in office at the time of filing, so exploratory committees or announcements with delayed paperwork would not count.
- **Market prices are weak evidence here.** The double-digit Polymarket figures for individual names are unverified, partly stale, and resolve on an announcement alone.
- **Some tail risk remains.** The field of openly interested sitting officials is large, and a quiet filing by an obscure member is possible.

Weighing the status quo heavily, I put this a little under one in ten.

Probability: 7%

## OUTSIDE VIEW

**Reference class:** Sitting governors, members of Congress or cabinet members who filed an FEC Statement of Candidacy for president before January 1 of the year preceding the election, and specifically in the final ~5 weeks of the midterm year.

**Base rate (from my own recollection, which differs in places from the research note):**
- **2008 cycle:** Yes. Gov. Tom Vilsack filed in November 2006 and Rep. Dennis Kucinich declared in December 2006.
- **2012 cycle:** No.
- **2016 cycle:** No. Jim Webb's November 2014 exploratory committee came from a former senator.
- **2020 cycle:** Arguably yes. I believe Rep. John Delaney was still a sitting congressman when he filed in mid-2017 (the research note says otherwise). Warren's exploratory committee paperwork came on Dec 31, 2018.
- **2024 cycle:** No.

Roughly 1–2 of the last 5 cycles saw a qualifying filing at some point before the pre-election year. But this question now covers only the last five weeks (Nov 24–Dec 31), since nothing has happened so far. Events in that specific window are rarer: Kucinich in 2006 and Warren in 2018 as a borderline case, so perhaps 1–1.5 of 5 cycles, and those came in more front-loaded cycles.

**Outside-view forecast:** about 10–15% for the remaining window.

## INSIDE VIEW

**(a) Time left:** About 5 weeks (Nov 24 to Dec 31, 2026), spanning Thanksgiving and Christmas.

**(b) Status quo:** No. No qualifying official has filed; only minor non-officeholders have.

**(c) No scenario:** Khanna decides "after the holidays" and launches in January or later. Kelly, Beshear and Newsom stick to conventional 2027 timelines. Bacon tours early states without filing. Any December move is a PAC, a draft committee or "testing the waters" activity without a Form 2.

**(d) Yes scenario:** A sitting official tries to seize first-mover advantage after the midterms. This could be Khanna accelerating, Beshear, or a long-shot House member (possibly a retiring one such as Bacon before Jan 3). They would file a Form 2, perhaps via an exploratory committee registered with the FEC in late December, as Warren did in 2018.

**Evidence adjustments:**
- **Khanna's explicit "after the holidays" timeline:** The most likely early mover is pointing outside the window. Moves down moderately.
- **No scheduled launches reported by any qualifying official:** Launches usually require weeks of staging and leak in advance. Moves down moderately.
- **DNC debates not until June 2027, with criteria coming in January:** There is little pressure to file in December. Moves down slightly.
- **Many sitting officials openly considering (Kelly, Beshear, Bacon, Khanna), plus a "Run Ro" draft committee:** A large pool creates tail risk of a surprise. Moves up slightly.
- **Prediction-market snippets (e.g., Beshear at 28%):** These are stale, unverified, and resolve on announcement alone rather than a Form 2 by a sitting official. Minimal weight.
- **Strict Form 2 requirement:** An announcement or testing-the-waters activity without the filing wouldn't count. Moves down slightly.
- **Fringe or quiet filing by a sitting House member:** Possible but none found. Adds a point or two.

Netting these, with heavy weight on the status quo and the short holiday-laden window, I land below the outside-view figure.

Probability: 5%

(b) **Status quo:** No. As of Nov 23, no sitting governor, senator, House member or cabinet member has filed a Form 2 for 2028. The only filers are minor figures without qualifying offices, such as Royce White and Christopher Campbell.

(c) **No scenario:** The likely contenders keep to their stated timelines.
- Khanna decides "after the holidays."
- Kelly decides "at the appropriate time."
- Beshear, Newsom and Bacon keep touring and building operations without formally becoming candidates.
- Launches cluster in early-to-mid 2027, ahead of the DNC debates that start in June 2027.

(d) **Yes scenario:** Someone moves early and files a Form 2 in December.
- A sitting official could try to claim first-mover status in a crowded post-midterm field. Khanna is the most likely, given his "more likely than not" comment and the draft committee.
- Beshear could do the same.
- A lame-duck member such as Bacon could file before his term ends on Jan 3.
- A fringe member could quietly file.
- An "exploratory committee" registered as a candidate committee would also count. Warren did this on Dec 31, 2018.

**Rationale:**
- **Base rates are mixed rather than near zero.** My research assistant's summary undercounts them.
  - John Delaney was still a sitting congressman when he announced and filed in July 2017.
  - Warren filed on Dec 31, 2018.
  - In the 2008 cycle, Vilsack (Nov 2006) and Kucinich (Dec 2006) launched while in office.
  - The 2016 and 2024 cycles had no qualifying filer this early.
  - So sitting officials filing in the post-midterm November–December window happens in perhaps 1–2 of the last 4–5 cycles.
- **The current evidence leans No.**
  - The only explicit timeline, from Khanna, points to January.
  - There is no reported launch scheduled before Dec 31.
  - The window includes the holidays.
  - Top-tier figures like Newsom have little incentive to file while still in office.
- **Some upside remains.** Several officials are openly weighing runs, a draft committee exists, and quiet filings from lesser-known members are possible.

Weighting the status quo heavily, I put this somewhat above a pure tail risk but well below even odds.

Probability: 13%
